title: See the tones inside a progression
context: C major · I → IV → V → I · root-position teaching voicings
caption: Synthetic I–IV–V–I in C major: C–E–G, F–A–C, G–B–D, then C–E–G. Step through the chord tones. These root-position voicings teach harmonic function; they are not an optimized voice-leading arrangement.

progression.label: I · C major
progression.comment: Tonic: C is the root, E the major third, and G the perfect fifth. These are three simultaneous chord tones.

progression.label: IV · F major
progression.comment: Subdominant: F–A–C. C is a shared pitch class with the tonic chord; its register can be changed when arranging.

progression.label: V · G major
progression.comment: Dominant: G–B–D. B can lead upward to C in a return to the tonic; actual voice movement depends on voicing.

progression.label: I · C major
progression.comment: Return to tonic. Audition alternate inversions in separate MIDI to explore smoother movement between voices.

actions.label: Ask agent: explain I–IV–V–I
actions.prompt: Explain the synthetic C-major progression I–IV–V–I using C–E–G, F–A–C and G–B–D. Explain chord tones and one possible smoother voicing without claiming these are detected chords in an owner's demo. Answer in the conversation language.
